German composer and organist, born in Eisenach in 1685 into a large family of musicians. He worked mostly in the service of courts and churches in Lutheran Germany, and from 1723 to his death in 1750 as music director at the St Thomas Church in Leipzig.

In Leipzig he wrote a new church cantata almost every week for years, as well as the St Matthew Passion and the Mass in B minor. Earlier, at the court of Köthen, he wrote the Brandenburg Concertos. His keyboard works, such as The Well-Tempered Clavier and the Goldberg Variations, are still the base of piano teaching. He was a master of counterpoint, weaving several melodies together at once.

In his lifetime he was known more as an organist than as a composer, and his style was thought old fashioned. After his death his music was played little, though Mozart and Beethoven studied it. A revival began in 1829 when Felix Mendelssohn conducted the St Matthew Passion in Berlin. Today he is seen as the summit of Baroque music.
